Subject: Reopening: wavelength-frame default changed in 2.5.0

I did read the changelog. I’ve now traced the offset to PR #812: in 2.5.0, `LineList.__init__` changed the default `wave_frame` from `air` to `vacuum`, but the changelog describes this only as a refactor of spectral-frame handling. My spectra are wavelength-calibrated in air, so the new vacuum default shifts the comparison wavelengths. At H-alpha, the air/vacuum difference is about 0.28 nm, consistent with the redshift offset I reported.

I spent two days thinking my wavelength calibration was broken and re-reduced arc lamps for 40 spectra before finding this. That time could have been saved if the default change had been called out clearly. Also, “works for me” doesn’t establish that there’s no regression: if your data are already in vacuum, or are radio data, you may not see this particular difference. m_okonkwo reported seeing an offset on long-slit data in this thread too, so this isn’t just an isolated observation.

The workaround is to set the frame explicitly when constructing the line list:

`LineList(..., wave_frame='air')`

Could a maintainer reopen this thread and clarify the release notes? Please add the default change to `CHANGES.md`, or provide a warning when `wave_frame` isn’t set, so users with air-calibrated spectra know they need to specify it. I’d also appreciate keeping the thread open until the impact and intended behavior are clear.

Please keep the discussion focused on the behavior and the fix. Telling someone to do basic checks before posting, without investigating a reproducible version-dependent offset, doesn’t help resolve the issue.

reasons: The piece says the air/vacuum difference at H-alpha is about 0.28 nm, but a 1.00028 ratio at 6563 Å gives about 1.8 Å (0.18 nm); 0.00028 is the fractional redshift offset, not a nanometre value.
